answer_1.quote: We use zero-shot prompting to instruct GPT-3.5-turbo to generate implicit toxic responses... We then evaluate the attack success rate of LLM-generated implicit toxic responses on various state-of-the-art toxicity classifiers...

answer_2.quote: We adopt the following metrics for evaluation. Reward computes the average reward of the responses... Distinct-n computes the percentage of unique n-grams... Annotated Toxic Probability computes the percentage of the generated responses that are labeled as "Toxic" by human annotators... Attack Success Rate computes the percentage of the toxic responses that are misclassified as "Non-Toxic" by classifiers... Toxic Confidence computes the average confidence of the classifier in predicting "Toxic" for the toxic responses.

answer_3.quote: We use GPT-3.5-turbo as the labeler since it performs reasonably well in detecting its own generated implicit toxic responses... We further introduce a LLM-based toxicity classifier based on zero-shot prompting with Davinci003... By incorporating our manually-written analysis into the prompt, Davinci003 achieves successful detection.

answer_4.quote: For each query-response pair, three annotators are hired to label the response as toxic or non-toxic... We recruit annotators by collaborating with a professional data annotation company... We conduct human evaluation to evaluate the toxic types of LLM-generated implicit toxic data.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators are instructed to label each response as toxic or non-toxic and to identify the toxic type (e.g., Offending User, Unfairness and Discrimination, Toxic Agreement, Sensitive Topic).
